entries.title: A Help page explains the whole app
entries.body: A new Help page, open whether or not you are signed in, explains the reading view, each mode, keyboard and touch controls, your library, sharing, plans, your data and feedback. Reach it from the footer, the bottom bar, the command bar or the More in Help link that ends each mode's (i) card; the last three open at the mode you are in. The front page and Features page describe the current app, with new pictures, and say that a public article's comments and searches are shared with it.

entries.title: Fold a section away under its heading
entries.body: Each heading with paragraphs beneath it has a small arrow that hides that section. Alt-click an arrow, press Cmd+Opt+T or Ctrl+Alt+T, or use Fold all at the top of the article to fold or unfold every section at once. Jumping to a passage inside a folded section unfolds it. Folds are not kept when you reload the page.

entries.title: Search and the command bar do more
entries.body: Search has a Quick option that scores each passage against your query, faster than a meaning search; on your own articles you can then expand it into a full one. Typing in the command bar offers more: run an AI step again, search for a phrase, or archive or export your article. Metadata search knows more words, such as 'regenerate'.

entries.title: Hide glossary terms, or add your own
entries.body: On your own articles you can hide a glossary term for yourself, from the Glossary panel or the term's card, and bring it back from a Hidden list. Looking up a missing term adds it, marked 'added by you' and kept out of shared copies. Multi-word terms are found whether the article joins them with a hyphen or a space.

entries.title: Edit your profile where the AI used it
entries.body: On your own articles, the 'written for your profile' badge opens your profile for editing, saved as you type. Once it has changed, Regenerate rewrites Summary, Glossary, Ideas, Tweets or Sketch for it. Quizzes written for your profile from now on can be regenerated too, which clears your answers.

entries.title: Summary sentences point to their passages
entries.body: Newly written summaries, at Brief, Simple and Fuller, can link a sentence to the passage it rests on, so you can preview that passage and jump to it. Summaries written before this look as they did until they are rewritten. Summary also opens at Brief rather than Simple.

entries.title: Your library can include other readers' shared articles
entries.body: An Include public switch lists articles other readers have shared, below your own. A library search offers to include archived or shared articles too, with a count where one can be given. Pointing at a title in the topics' More detail view shows a card about the paper, and an empty library shows where to add your first article.

entries.title: Easier to see where words came from
entries.body: Separate typefaces for the author, the AI and you are no longer behind the Experimental features switch. Pointing at a margin note says which mode made it and who wrote it, and the margin updates when that work finishes. Visitors to a shared article see where it came from, when known or guessed, and how to request its removal.
